turns.en: But I do see more startups, more opportunities to raise money and build your own ideas.
turns.zh: 但我确实看到更多初创公司，也看到更多融资和打造自己创意的机会。

turns.en: Now, yeah, I totally agree. It's like there was a line—this is my economic brain thinking—but you know, there was a literal line on a graph where if you could not generate this much profit based on this problem, it's not worth pursuing. It doesn't make financial sense to do this. And that line has just fallen. So there's a whole subset, there's this whole category of problems that previously nobody had the financial incentive to solve that are just wide open. Look around you, like local businesses. Oh my goodness. There's so many problems that anybody listening to this is totally capable of solving on their own, fully. Take a shot.
turns.zh: 现在，我完全同意。就好像有一条线——这是我用经济学头脑想的——你知道，图表上真的有一条线：如果你不能从某个问题上赚到这么多利润，那就不值得去做。这在财务上讲不通。而那条线刚刚跌落了。所以有一整个子集、一整个类别的难题，以前没有人有经济动机去解决，现在完全敞开了。环顾四周，比如本地小生意。天哪。有太多问题，任何听众都完全有能力自己解决，彻底解决。放手一试吧。

turns.en: Take a shot. Yes, yes, I like it. Well, I can't think of a better line to end on than take your shot.
turns.zh: 放手一试。是的，是的，我喜欢这个说法。好吧，我想不出比你的“放手一试”更好的收尾了。

turns.en: And, uh, Louie, I appreciate you coming on and giving us a little bit of the insider scoop, but also just telling it how it is, because I think you're feeling this like everybody else, you know, it's a crazy time. And sometimes it's good to just shine a light on the reality. And I appreciate you coming on today and doing that with us. It's always fun. Thank you very much.
turns.zh: 呃，Louie，我很感激你上节目，给我们一些内幕消息，也把实际情况讲出来。因为我觉得你和其他人一样有这种感受，你知道，这是个疯狂的时代。有时候我们应该把现实照亮，所以我感谢你今天来和我们做这件事。这总是很有趣。非常感谢。

turns.en: Before I let you go, I want to take just one minute to run you through my favorite products, because I'm constantly asked what's in my stack. Framer is how I build websites. Genway is how I do research. Granola is how I take notes during crit. Jitter is how I animate my designs. Lovable is how I build my ideas in code. Mabin is how I find design inspiration. Paper is how I design like a creative. And Raycast is my shortcut every step of the way. Now, I've hand-selected these companies so that I can do these episodes full-time. So, by far, the number one way to support the show is to check them out. You can find the full list at dive.club/partners.
turns.zh: 在你走之前，我想用一分钟介绍我最喜欢的产品，因为我经常被问到我的技术栈里有什么。Framer 是我的建站工具。Genway 是我做研究的方式。Granola 是我在评审时做笔记的工具。Jitter 是我给设计做动效的工具。Lovable 是我用代码实现想法的方式。Mabin 是我寻找设计灵感的地方。Paper 是我像创意人一样设计的工具。而 Raycast 是我每个步骤的快捷方式。我亲手挑选了这些公司，这样我才能全职做这些节目。所以，到目前为止，支持这个节目最好的方式就是去看看它们。你可以在 dive.club/partners 找到完整列表。

consensus.en: Design systems have become the centerpiece of engineering work; AI code generation depends on them to produce quality output.
consensus.zh: 设计系统已成为工程工作的核心；AI代码生成依赖它们来产出高质量成果。

consensus.en: Documentation and guidelines are no longer just for humans; they are the foundation for predictable AI workflows.
consensus.zh: 文档和指南不再仅仅面向人；它们是可预测AI工作流的基础。

consensus.en: Cross-functional collaboration is expanding as designers, engineers, and PMs contribute across phases instead of working in silos.
consensus.zh: 跨职能协作正在扩展，设计师、工程师和产品经理在不同阶段共同贡献，而非各自为政。

consensus.en: Quality bar is everyone's responsibility, and a design system is that bar, not a siloed team's job.
consensus.zh: 质量标杆是每个人的责任，设计系统就是那个标杆，而不是某个孤立团队的职责。

consensus.en: AI tools enable non-technical designers to iterate faster from canvas to browser, deepening their involvement in product decisions.
consensus.zh: AI工具使非技术设计师能更快地从画布迭代到浏览器，加深他们对产品决策的参与。

consensus.en: The new workflow is start from anywhere—code, canvas, or document—then bounce between tools to refine ideas.
consensus.zh: 新的工作方式是“从任何地方开始”——代码、画布或文档——然后在工具间跳跃来完善想法。

contrarian.en: The claim that design systems are dead is wrong; they matter more than ever for AI-driven development.
contrarian.zh: “设计系统已死”的说法是错误的；在AI驱动的开发中，它们比以往更重要。

contrarian.en: Contrary to popular jargon, prototypes are not the new PRDs; writing documents remains the best way to gain buy-in before pixels.
contrarian.zh: 与流行说法相反，原型不是新的PRD；在动像素之前，写文档仍是获得认可的最佳方式。

contrarian.en: Over-tokenization can be counterproductive; raw values may be acceptable for experiments, and systems should adapt.
contrarian.zh: 过度使用token可能适得其反；在实验中原始值可以接受，系统需要适应变化。

contrarian.en: Long-term career planning is fruitless in this fast-changing landscape; taking shots and enjoying the process matters more.
contrarian.zh: 在这个快速变化的环境中，长期职业规划是徒劳的；抓住机会并享受过程更重要。

contrarian.en: Most software is mediocre, and many users don't care about pixels; designers should prioritize business outcomes over visual perfection.
contrarian.zh: 大多数软件很平庸，许多用户并不在乎像素；设计师应优先考虑业务成果而非视觉完美。

contrarian.en: Role blurring isn't just cost-cutting; front-end development will eventually be recognized as part of UX design.
contrarian.zh: 角色模糊不只是为了削减成本；前端开发最终会被视为UX设计的一部分。
